concreteFindings.finding: The driver checks kind=development and pair completeness, but never requires exactly 20 unique concepts, 40 pairs, 80 unique slots, or unique slot IDs. A self-consistent newly hashed development manifest with omitted or duplicated concepts/slots is accepted and its smaller or duplicated ledger becomes the reported denominator.
concreteFindings.smallestRegression: Construct a freshly hashed development manifest with 19 concepts or duplicate slotId values and assert planLocalCampaign refuses it.

concreteFindings.finding: A destination without a campaign receipt is recovered from run.json/request.json semantics and SVG bytes, but those files contain no campaign requestId or toolingHash. Old or copied output produced by different generator bytes at the same concept/master destination can pass recovery under a current lock.
concreteFindings.smallestRegression: Place semantically matching terminal output lacking the current requestId/toolingHash in a locked destination and assert recovery refuses it; bind those identities into a pre-dispatch marker or generator receipt.

concreteFindings.finding: Dry-run scheduled is always requests.slice(0,maxRequests). It does not exclude identity-validated terminal receipts, so a resume dry-run reports already completed pairs instead of the requests execute mode would charge next.
concreteFindings.smallestRegression: Persist a validated first receipt, dry-run with maxRequests=1, and require scheduled[0] to be the next pending request.

concreteFindings.finding: The lock fingerprints repository production files and command/model strings, but not the Codex and Claude executable bytes or reported versions. Replacing either executable at the same path/name preserves the campaign identity.
concreteFindings.smallestRegression: Change a fixture author binary at the same path and assert the planned tooling identity changes, or explicitly record this as an environment limitation.
